what: observe: tell the stall watchdog a query ran (Andrew, 2026-10-31: the stall watchdog). The daemon's watchdog fails a request when nothing has moved for 60 s while its tasks run: no info span closed, no task ended. A long front-end check can run for minutes inside one task with no info span closing. So once per query execution (a real run, not a memo hit), call blaze_profile::moved(): a thread-local read and one relaxed add on the thread's own cache line, no allocation, no lock. Put it where a query's function is about to run or has just run. It needs `blaze-profile.workspace = true` in blaze-query's Cargo.toml (deps: rustc-hash, serde, serde_json, tracing, object, rustc-demangle; no salsa or hir). Without it, a check that runs over 60 s with every thread inside queries is a false stall.

history.note: applied, not yet run: blaze-query cannot depend on blaze-profile (cycle through blaze-v2-proof), so blaze-query lib.rs has `on_each_run(hook: fn())` (a OnceLock<fn()>, one Acquire load per run, nothing on a hit), called in db/function.rs right after F::execute. Test db/tests.rs each_run_is_told_and_no_hit_is. Registration `blaze_query::on_each_run(blaze_profile::moved)` queued to cargo for the daemon start.
